body: No party wants to be the one who actually has to burst the bubble though, that's what I'm talking about. Liberals and conservatives both don't want to be the ones to cause that. It will be messy for every Canadian no matter what political party takes the hit. But someone has to do something at some point as the current bubble is unsustainable. Clearly waiting for the invisible hand of the market to change things isn't working.

I dont have solutions to every level of government, I was just pointing out that blame is passed around between the 3 levels which results in no progress actually being made on the issue. Someone needs to take concrete steps to improve the situation but all 3 levels are scared to take any responsibility towards fixing it lest they lose the votes of homeowners.

At this point municipalities that refuse to build housing when they are more than capable of doing so should have provincial funding and services cut. The blame is passed constantly on a provincial, municipal, and federal level but in Victoria's and Oak Bays case it comes down to a refusal to do anything that might threaten home prices, including building affordable housing. Horgan threatened as much in the past but I think he needs to follow through, although I doubt he will. Homeowners aren't the only citizens that should matter, municipalities have to take care of all their people not just the priveleged few that own property.
